activity.notes: The user supplied Ahiram with the parenthetical label Phoenicia. ATLAS normalizes the political authority to the Kingdom of Byblos rather than a unitary Phoenicia: Ahiram's own royal sarcophagus inscription identifies him as king of Byblos/Gebal, and Oxford describes Byblos as a major Phoenician city and an independent kingdom. Absolute chronology is reconstructed rather than directly dated. DEAPS summarizes major scholarly schemes that place Ahiram around 1000 BCE and his son/successor Ittobaal around 980–975 BCE. ATLAS therefore uses c.1000–c.980 BCE as a conservative representative reign window with both endpoints approximate; it is not asserted as an exact accession/death span.

sources.title: Byblos — Oxford Classical Dictionary
sources.citation_text: The Oxford Classical Dictionary describes Byblos as a major port of Phoenicia, notes the sarcophagus of King Ahiram as a tenth-century BCE royal monument, and identifies Byblos as an independent kingdom.
